newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy parlt votes down STET transfer.
newsitem.headline: Italy parlt votes down STET transfer.

text.p: The lower house of parliament on Wednesday voted against a government plan to transfer control of Italian telecommunications gaint STET to the treasury from state holding group IRI.

The government last year decided to take STET into the treasury fold ahead of its privatisation, which is slated for later this year. The transfer would have also enabled the government to reduce IRI debt in accordance with a European Union deal.
The government decree was voted down by a very narrow margin in the Chamber of Deputies.

It was defeated after the hard-left Communist Refoundation, which guarantees Prodi's majority in the the lower house, abstained and centre-right oppostion parties mustered enough votes to deliever the shock defeat.
Communist Refoundation is ideologically opposed to the STET privatisation.

Massimo D'Alema, head of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), the largest party in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition, said the vote was a very serious seback and hoped that the government could find a way to remedy the situation.
The Treasury said last month it would pay at least 14.53 trillion lire ($9.3 billion) to debt-laden IRI to take over its controlling stake in STET.
The transfer of shares from IRI to the Treasury was outlined in November when Italy abruptly announced that its forthcoming privatisation of STET would not go ahead in 1996 as had been planned.
The Treasury was to have paid IRI three trillion lire by the end of January and hand over the balance by the end of June 1997.
The cash was to be used exclusively to cut IRI's huge debt pile. IRI holds 61.27 percent of ordinary shares in STET, Europe's fourth-biggest phone company.
STET acts as a telecommunications holding and in turn controls Telecom Italia, the operating unit.
Under a 1993 accord with the European Union, IRI must cut its debt to below five trillion lire by the end of the year from its end-1995 level of 22.5 trillion.
The government is currently working on plans to fuse STET with Telecom Italia. Rome newsroom -- 39-6-678-2501
